status.en: 102 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 25% fewer than the week before, most of them in Islamabad, Kabul and Balochistan.
status.nb: 102 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 25 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Islamabad, Kabul og Belutsjistan.

summary.en: Pakistan’s security forces have responded to unprovoked fire from Afghan Taliban posts in South Waziristan, killing a civilian and wounding five, and have also carried out operations against illegal Afghans in Peshawar. Taliban fighters clashed with Pakistani forces in Paktika, leaving three dead and injured. In Balochistan, a woman suffered burns in an acid attack by her brother-in-law and tribal protests erupted after gunmen killed three people. The conflict has caused 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistans sikkerhetsstyrker har svart på uprovokert ild fra afghanske Taliban-poster i Sør-Waziristan, der drepte en sivil og såret fem, og har også gjennomført operasjoner mot ulovlige afghanere i Peshawar. Taliban-krigere kom i konflikt med pakistanske styrker i Paktika, noe som førte til tre døde og sårede. I Balochistan fikk en kvinne brannskader i et syreangrep fra sin svoger, og stammeprotester brøt ut etter at væpnede menn drepte tre personer. Konflikten har forårsaket 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
